title: Retained candidates are bounded
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let $\tau\in\mathbb{Q}$ satisfy $0<\tau\le1$, let $E$ assign a rational estimate to each restricted Fourier weight, and let $k<n$ be a natural number. Let $A$ be a finite family of subsets of the first $n$ coordinates. Assume that every set in $A$ is contained in the first $k$ coordinates; that for every frequency set $U$, if $\tau\le|\widehat f(U)|$, then the part of $U$ among the first $k$ coordinates belongs to $A$; and that, when $k>0$, every $S\in A$ has restricted Fourier weight greater than $\tau^2/4$ on the first $k$ coordinates. Also assume that on every candidate formed from $A$ by either keeping a set or adjoining coordinate $k$, the estimate for its part among the first $k+1$ coordinates differs from the corresponding restricted Fourier weight by less than $\tau^2/4$. Then the number of such candidates whose estimated weight is greater than $\tau^2/2$ is at most $\lceil4/\tau^2\rceil$.
